festivals: Maha Shivaratri (seven-day festival at the nearby Mahabaleshwar Temple)

history.dynasty: Traditional (unverified; idol popularly dated ~1500 years old - weakly sourced)
history.summary: Honours the boy Ganesha of the Atma-linga legend: the boy who, at the gods' behest, tricked Ravana into setting down Shiva's Atma-linga at Gokarna, then 'turned to stone' here. The temple stands a few yards from the Mahabaleshwar Temple at the start of Car Street, and Gokarna pilgrims customarily visit it first before the main shrine. The idol's age is popularly given as ~1500 years (weakly sourced - verify); sources CONFLICT on the idol being two-handed with a hole on the head (said to mark the stone Ravana threw at him) versus four-handed holding lotus, a bowl of sweets, a noose and a goad. Also known as Sidda Ganapati. It is the starting point of the Maha Shivaratri Ratha Yatra. Coordinates are approximate (a few yards from the Mahabaleshwar Temple).

name: Maha Ganapati Temple
town_description: Gokarna is a coastal temple town in Uttara Kannada district, Karnataka, on the Arabian Sea between the Gangavalli and Aganashini rivers. One of the seven Mukti Sthalas of Karnataka and revered as Dakshina Kashi, it draws Shaivite pilgrims year-round while its beaches and the Konkan Railway have also made it popular with domestic and foreign travellers. The town pairs a traditional pilgrim economy - the Koti Tirtha, Car Street and the daily temple routine - with beaches such as Om Beach and Kudle, treks and a traveller cafe scene.

travel.airport: Dabolim Airport (GOI), Goa - ~140 km; taxi/bus ~3.5-4 hrs (verify)
travel.railway: Gokarna Road (GOK) on the Konkan Railway - ~8-10 km from town (some sources say 6 km) (verify); Ankola ~20 km, Kumta ~30 km have more trains
travel.road: NH 66 passes nearby; KSRTC and private buses from Bengaluru (~475 km), Mangalore (~240 km), Hubli and Panjim (Goa); autos/taxis within town

visitor_information.best_time: October to March (cool season); Ganesh Chaturthi draws a large influx
visitor_information.opening_hours: Commonly cited as early morning to midday and late afternoon to early evening (verify locally); no entry fee; photography inside may be restricted
